newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan April leading index 5.6, coincident 10.0.
newsitem.headline: Japan April leading index 5.6, coincident 10.0.

text.p: Japan's diffusion index of leading economic indicators stood at 5.6 on a scale of 100 in April, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said on Friday.
The EPA said in a statement that Japan's economic recovery remained intact despite weakness seen in the index of leading indicators.
A breakdown of the indices of economic indicators follows:
The index of leading indicators was below 50 for a fourth consecutive month in April.
The index of coincident indicators fell below 50 for the first time in eight months, while the lagging indicators index was below 50 for the first time in two months.

A figure below 50, the so-called "boom-or-bust" mark, for the index of leading economic indicators is generally taken as suggesting the economy will contract in the coming months, while a figure above 50 suggests the economy will expand.
The coincident index measures current economic conditions, while the lagging index traces economic trends in the past few months.
